whatItIs.heading: What is professional mold testing?
whatItIs.body:
Mold testing is a diagnostic process that answers two specific questions: is mold present, and what species and concentration is it? The answers come from laboratory analysis of air and surface samples collected on-site—not from a visual assessment alone.

Air sampling captures airborne spore counts in each tested room and compares them to an outdoor baseline. Surface swabs and tape lifts identify what species are growing on a specific material. Samples are submitted to an accredited independent laboratory; results typically return within two to four business days. The final report identifies species, spore concentrations, and the comparison to baseline that helps distinguish a normal indoor environment from one requiring remediation.

Mold testing is diagnostic, not remediation. Testing determines scope and guides the remediation plan—it does not clean or remove mold. If testing confirms elevated levels, mold remediation is the next step.

steps.title: On-site scoping and sample plan
steps.body: A Gallagher technician walks the property, identifies areas of concern, and establishes a sampling plan. Every test includes at least one outdoor baseline air sample so indoor counts can be compared against local ambient conditions—a step that distinguishes a meaningful elevation from normal outdoor variation.

steps.title: Air sampling and surface collection
steps.body: Spore trap cassettes collect air samples in each area under review. Surface swabs or tape lift samples are collected from visible growth or staining. Samples are sealed, labeled, and submitted to an accredited third-party lab within 24 hours of collection.

steps.title: Laboratory analysis
steps.body: The accredited lab analyzes each sample, identifies mold species present, quantifies spore concentrations, and returns results within two to four business days. Lab fees are included in the testing cost—no separate invoice from the lab.

steps.title: Written report and recommendations
steps.body: Gallagher delivers a written report that presents the lab findings in plain language: which species were found, at what concentrations, how those numbers compare to the outdoor baseline, and what action—if any—is warranted. If remediation is indicated, the report serves as the scope basis.

signs.heading: Situations that call for professional mold testing
signs.intro: Mold testing answers the question before committing to remediation—or confirms there is nothing to remediate. These are the most common situations that warrant it.

items.title: Pre-purchase home inspection revealed moisture or mold concerns
items.body: A home inspector who flags elevated moisture readings or possible mold needs confirmation before closing. Mold testing provides the documentation buyers and their lenders require.

items.title: Tenant or landlord dispute involving mold claims
items.body: A third-party lab report with documented species and spore counts is the standard of evidence in California tenant-landlord disputes involving mold. Neither party's verbal account substitutes for lab data.

items.title: Unexplained health symptoms without visible mold
items.body: Persistent respiratory irritation, allergic responses, or fatigue that correlates with time spent in the home but lacks an obvious cause can be investigated through air quality testing. Elevated indoor spore counts—even without visible growth—explain many such patterns.

items.title: Post-remediation confirmation
items.body: Clearance testing after a mold remediation project confirms that spore counts returned to baseline before containment is removed and the space is re-occupied. This is the standard endpoint for every Gallagher remediation job.

items.title: Past water damage in an area without professional drying
items.body: Any area that experienced a plumbing leak, roof intrusion, or flooding that was not professionally dried within 48 to 72 hours carries a high risk of mold colonization inside wall cavities. Testing confirms whether that risk materialized.

whyUs.heading: Why Southern California homeowners choose Gallagher for mold testing
whyUs.body:
Mold testing produces usable results only when the sampling protocol is correct. Sampling from the wrong location, using the wrong cassette type for the question being asked, or omitting the outdoor baseline produces data that is difficult to interpret and may not be accepted by insurers, attorneys, or real estate transactions.

Gallagher Restoration Co. has performed mold assessments across Southern California for more than 15 years. IICRC-trained technicians design each sample plan around the specific question—pre-purchase, tenant dispute, health concern, post-remediation clearance—rather than applying a generic protocol. All samples go to an accredited third-party laboratory; the independence of the lab matters when results need to hold up to scrutiny. The written report translates lab data into a clear action recommendation. If remediation is indicated, Gallagher can move directly from testing into remediation without a contractor handoff. Call (951) 541-0034 to schedule testing; same-day and next-day appointments are available across the five-county area.

pricing.heading: Mold testing pricing—what to expect
pricing.body: Mold testing in Southern California typically ranges from $350 to $1,200. The lower end covers a focused test—two to four air samples in a single area of concern plus the outdoor baseline. The upper end reflects a comprehensive multi-room test across a larger property or a job requiring a higher number of samples to adequately characterize a complex situation. Lab fees are included in the quoted price; there is no separate laboratory invoice. The initial on-site assessment to scope the test is provided at no charge. If testing results indicate that mold remediation is needed, Gallagher Restoration Co. applies the testing documentation directly to the remediation scope—no need to start the process over with a separate contractor.

faqs.q: What is the difference between mold testing and mold inspection?
faqs.a: A mold inspection is a visual and moisture-based assessment—a trained technician looks for visible mold, checks moisture readings, and identifies conditions that favor mold growth. Mold testing adds laboratory sampling: air and surface samples submitted to an accredited lab that returns a report identifying species and spore concentrations. Inspection tells you where to look; testing tells you what is there and at what level. Many situations call for both.

faqs.q: How accurate are mold test kits from hardware stores?
faqs.a: Consumer test kits from hardware stores have two known limitations: they do not include an outdoor baseline for comparison, and they are not analyzed by an accredited laboratory. The result tells you mold spores exist—which is true of virtually every indoor environment—without telling you whether the indoor concentration is elevated relative to normal outdoor levels. Professional testing with an accredited lab provides the comparison data that makes the result actionable.

faqs.q: How long does it take to get mold test results?
faqs.a: Standard laboratory turnaround for mold spore analysis is two to four business days after samples are submitted. Rush analysis is available from most accredited labs at an additional fee and returns results within 24 hours. Gallagher Restoration Co. submits samples within 24 hours of collection and delivers the written report within one business day of receiving lab results.

faqs.q: Does homeowners insurance cover mold testing in California?
faqs.a: Coverage for mold testing depends on the policy and the cause of the mold. When testing is part of a documented claim involving a covered water loss—a burst pipe or appliance failure, for example—testing costs are typically included in the claim. Standalone testing without a documented covered loss is generally not covered. Gallagher Restoration Co. can advise on documentation requirements during the initial consultation.
